figure_alt.Z11-P63: Left: a caller kneels beside a person who is unresponsive, breathing abnormally or bleeding severely, calls at once on a phone and keeps giving care while talking, saying the location first: trail, landmark or coordinates with their format. Centre: if the call drops, dispatch already has the location. Right: a six-item report card filled in before the trip (location and last known point, people and injuries, breathing, bleeding and warmth, access hazards, shelter, water and battery, stay-put plan and callback number) and completed while help is on the way; it is never a reason to delay the call. Conceptual, not to scale.
figure_alt.Z04-P51: Left: water that is bottled or boiled and cooled feeds drinking, tooth brushing, washing produce, making ice and washing dishes; wounds are rinsed only with clean potable water or sterile saline. Upper right: infant formula follows its own rules. Ready-to-feed formula is safest, especially for infants under 2 months, born prematurely or with a weakened immune system. Powdered formula is not sterile, so safe water alone does not make it safe; follow current CDC directions for the infant. Under a chemical advisory, boiling does not help: use bottled water or ready-to-feed. Lower right: a Do Not Use notice means no tap contact at all. Conceptual, not to scale.
figure_alt.Z13-P49: A solid-waste bucket lined with two heavy bags, with dry cover material such as sawdust added after each use and a tight lid; a separate bucket for liquids; and a handwashing station with a spigot jug, soap and a catch basin right beside them. Hands are washed with soap and safe water after every use; alcohol rub does not replace handwashing after toilet, diaper or vomit tasks. Tied bags go into a lidded outdoor bin for disposal under local health rules, away from food areas, wells, gardens and storm drains. Conceptual, not to scale.
figure_alt.Z13-P50: Left: a spigot jug on a stand pours a thin stream of safe water over soapy hands into a catch basin, so a 20-second soap wash uses little water; the basin is emptied away from wells and food gardens. Right: after using the toilet, changing a diaper, cleaning up vomit or handling waste, and before handling food, wash with soap and water; hand sanitizer does not work well against norovirus and is not a substitute. Sanitizer with at least 60 percent alcohol is an interim fallback only when soap and water truly are unavailable and hands are not visibly dirty; saving water does not make it equivalent. Disposable plates save potable water. Conceptual, not to scale.
figure_alt.Z11-P32: Plan-view box detour around a compact obstacle: four 90-degree turns, an offset leg counted in paces, a return leg paced to the same distance with extra paces where slope or brush shortens the stride, and a regained line that stays approximate until checked against the map. A matching count does not confirm position. Conceptual, not to scale.
